overview: F4290 is the formation check event, so the discussion should be cumulative without becoming a memory dump. Be ready to brief the maneuver contracts, safety stop criteria, formation emergency roles, and the method used to review applicable emergency procedures and N/W/Cs.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion Items

items.text: Treat any previously discussed maneuver as a review of contracts, checkpoints, and discontinue criteria rather than a list of isolated steps.

children.text: For departure work, review lineup, interval takeoff, section takeoff, initial rendezvous, and abort responsibilities.
For parade work, review A-B-C corrections, parade turns into and away, crossunder, breakup and rendezvous, underrun, and lead change.
For recovery work, review cruise-to-parade transition, speed brake coordination, section approaches, break spacing, NORDO recovery, and section missed approach.
For cruise maneuvering, review 60-degree bearing, step-down, lead/lag/pure pursuit, terminate, and knock-it-off criteria.
Brief the setup, the visual references, the correction priority, and the common unsafe trend for each maneuver.
Know which aircraft owns deconfliction at each point and when Lead must be directive.
Use terminate for expected training stops, knock-it-off for safety concerns, and underrun when a rendezvous geometry is unsafe.

items.text: Any emergency procedure means the student must show a repeatable review method, not invent an exhaustive list during the brief.

children.text: Start with aircraft control and the applicable NATOPS critical action or checklist.
Add the N/W/Cs that change the decision, timing, or crew coordination.
State whether the emergency is handled as individual aircraft, section support, lost sight, blind, NORDO, Section PEL, airborne damaged aircraft, or down-aircraft response.
Preserve formation separation before trying to preserve flight integrity.
Aviate: maintain aircraft control and execute the correct emergency procedure.
Communicate: use the correct aircraft call sign when one aircraft has the emergency, then be directive on tactical and ATC frequencies.
Separate: transfer lead, move to perch, detach, climb, turn away, or establish altitude separation as the emergency requires.
Recover: choose a suitable field or pattern, coordinate support, and avoid rejoining damaged aircraft unless specifically directed and safe.

studyNotes.summary: F4290 should be studied as a cumulative formation check: know the maneuver contracts, know the stop criteria, and use a disciplined emergency review method with N/W/Cs.

summary: F4290 is the formation check-flight discussion set for cumulative maneuver review and emergency-procedure review method.
title: Formation Check Flight
